subject.title: [Feature]: Store configuration backup files in their own directory, with datetime name convention

question: Should core config backups move to a dedicated `config-backup/` directory, or should OpenClaw keep adjacent backups and route only datetime naming through the existing timestamp issue and PR?
rationale: The source change is feasible, but the layout choice affects recovery, sensitive backup permissions, legacy adjacent backup retention, audit output, docs, and overlapping timestamp-only work.

options.title: Adopt dedicated directory layout
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical design and require an upgrade-safe implementation that moves backups into a directory while preserving recovery, permissions, retention, docs, and tests.

options.title: Limit scope to timestamp suffixes
options.body: Keep backups adjacent and route only the naming work through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39923 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/40392, then close or narrow this directory request separately.

options.title: Keep current backup ring
options.body: Reject the layout and naming change for now and document the adjacent numbered ring as intended behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt dedicated directory layout
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical design and require an upgrade-safe implementation that moves backups into a directory while preserving recovery, permissions, retention, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history and review context across config backup, recovery, and tests.
